spans.text: ■FILE■ PACC78493721879619, decrypting...
Beep.
An audio recording starts playing.
Hello, Washington D.C. Police Department.
How may I help you?
My ex-wife took my daughter!
Sir, please tell me about your daughter.
Her name is Sana! She just turned six! She can't leave her father! That woman must've kidnapped her!
By "that woman", are you referring to your ex-wife? Please also tell me about her and yourself.
My name is Shaun. Shaun Rodriguez.
My ex-wife is called Martha. We were officially divorced two months ago, and I was given custody of Sana.
She took Sana while I was at work today!
Are you certain it was Ms. Martha who took Sana and not anyone else?
Absolutely. The CCTV camera at my door shows Martha coming back for her stuff. Sana opened the door for her even though I warned her not to let that woman in!
Then they left together.
So Sana was taken away by her own mother?
Yes.

Mr. Rodriguez, we now have a general understanding of the situation. Please come to the station to submit your divorce agreement or court ruling, and we will provide supporting evidence for your legal claim.
Aren't you going to find my daughter?
I know Martha booked the earliest flight to the Neo-Soviet Union—she's going to take Sana with her...
Apologies, Mr. Rodriguez. According to the law, we have no authority to prevent Ms. Martha from taking her daughter out of the country.
We advise you to take legal action. If Ms. Martha has already left the country, you can apply for international legal assistance, and we will help provide supporting evidence.
Also, I'd like to confirm—did Sana or Ms. Martha leave any messages for you?
Martha cut off all contact with me long ago. Sana...
Sana left me a note.
Did the note say where she was going?
She wrote, "Mama has nothing left. I want to be with Mama."
Based on the note, Sana went with Ms. Martha voluntarily. There's no indication that Ms. Martha took her by force.
You don't understand! Sana is only six—she doesn't know anything! That woman must have forced her to write that note!
She can't possibly take good care of Sana! She's a workaholic with no human emotions—how could she possibly sacrifice time or energy for a child?!
Mr. Rodriguez, please calm down.
Calm down? My daughter has followed that devil to hell—how do you expect me to calm down?!
Sana's life is just beginning, and she's already made the worst possible choice!
She shouldn't be in some backwater town in the Neo-Soviet Union, scorned by ignorant locals—she should be at Sidwell Friends School, growing up alongside the future elite of America!
Sorry, sir. Please come to the station once you've calmed down, and then—
Thud.
The caller hangs up vehemently.
